header.description: Labelled query set for durable output search (R16). Queries are phrased from symptoms, issue text or a paraphrase, not doc titles. Recall test counts a query as found when at least one path in `relevant` is in the top 5 hits.

fields.query: text a searcher would type; the only input any ranker or baseline run sees
fields.relevant: repo-relative paths under docs/solutions/ (never README or _archived/). A superseded doc's successor is labelled too.
fields.split: `tune` (tuning may read it) or `heldout` (report only); fixed before any ranker existed
fields.lexical_reachable: true when a relevant doc's title, symptoms, tags or module shares a query token of 3 or more characters (frontmatter, not body text). false means no such shared token.
fields.source: `issue` (wording from a real GitHub issue), `paraphrase` (how someone would describe the problem, not the doc's words) or `symptoms` (taken from a doc's symptoms)
fields.token_overlap: present on the #820 entry only: overlap of the query with the target's title, tags, module and component

authoring_rules: The #820 query was written from the issue wording and saved before the target doc's frontmatter was opened. Its token overlap was recorded afterwards and `lexical_reachable` is pinned true.
The #820 overlap is stopwords only (a, not, the), with zero content words. It tests the symptom-vocabulary gap, not tag matching.
Splits were fixed before any ranker existed: 5 heldout (including #820), 14 tune.
Source mix: 7 issue, 10 paraphrase, 2 symptoms. 13 of 14 tune queries are issue or paraphrase.
3 queries are lexical_reachable false (q03, q12, q16).
Authored blind to any ranker. Labels were kept outside the repo until the R17 grep baseline finished. No query or label was changed after the baseline run.

queries.query: reviewers found the same defect but anchored at different lines in a prose file, so the duplicate findings are not merged and the agreement boost never fires

token_overlap.tokenizer: lowercase ASCII [a-z0-9] runs; underscore/hyphen-joined runs also emit the whole identifier and each part
token_overlap.note: Overlap is stopwords only (a, not, the). No content word of the query appears in the target title, tags, module or component, so the query tests the symptom-vocabulary gap, not tag matching. Pinned lexical_reachable=true per plan.

queries.query: Discovered user skills lose their agent, model and subtask fields on OpenCode v1
old links go to a missing document after deploying under a subpath
`which opencode` succeeds while `opencode --version` fails and real-host integration tests run instead of skipping
a regular expression hangs on input with many repeated opening markers and no end marker
ce:review merge fails with "internal error in merge" when surviving findings exceed 32
A managed `skills` list on v1 denies the allowed skills when they are loaded through `systematic_skill`
Typecheck never covers tests/ or scripts/
Large edit or write arguments make the workflow guard unavailable
OpenCode compaction.prune can clear loaded systematic_skill output
bot comments on pull requests in my own repo get ignored and the run claims it is a fork
automation finished happily yet customers cannot obtain what got shipped
Could not parse expression with acorn, and the error points at a heading line
my one-line docs fix keeps getting undone after I run the tests
the integrity report crashes instead of listing problems because one document has a self-referencing metadata value
pull request text posted from a shell script has stray slashes in front of code formatting marks
new worktree helper creates its folder beside the wrong git directory when the repository uses a separate git dir
I added the plugin to my opencode config but the new major version silently ignores it
dependency bot upgrade PRs fail the required test because an assertion hardcodes a commit hash
